about: Authored destination notes for kahan-chalein: what is in a city, and what the last mile looks like. Editorial content, written for this project — not harvested data. Distances are approximate planning figures.

profiles.name: New Delhi
profiles.why: The capital, and the densest cluster of monuments in the country.

profiles.name: Old Delhi
profiles.why: Mughal Delhi: the Red Fort, the great mosque, and the lanes of Chandni Chowk.

profiles.name: Delhi Nizamuddin
profiles.why: The Sufi dargah and the tomb that gave Humayun’s architecture its rehearsal.

profiles.name: Agra
profiles.why: The Taj Mahal, with a fort and a tomb that most day-trippers run out of time for.

gateways.name: Fatehpur Sikri
gateways.note: bus or taxi from Agra Cantt, about an hour

profiles.name: Agra (Fort side)
profiles.why: The fort end of Agra: the station is a walk from the fort and the river.

profiles.name: Mathura
profiles.why: Krishna’s birthplace, with Vrindavan half an hour by road.

gateways.name: Vrindavan
gateways.note: auto or bus; the temple circuit needs half a day

profiles.name: Varanasi
profiles.why: The ghats at dawn, and one of the oldest continuously lived-in cities anywhere.

gateways.name: Sarnath
gateways.note: auto or bus; where the Buddha gave his first sermon

profiles.name: Sarnath
profiles.why: The deer park where Buddhism began to be taught, with its stupa and museum.

profiles.name: Prayagraj
profiles.why: The Sangam, where the Ganga and Yamuna meet — the Kumbh city.

profiles.name: Ayodhya
profiles.why: The Ram Janmabhoomi temple town on the Sarayu.

profiles.name: Lucknow
profiles.why: Awadhi architecture and Awadhi food, both at their best here.

profiles.name: Kanpur
profiles.why: A leather-and-industry city on the Ganga; the big junction of the Kanpur–Delhi trunk.

profiles.name: Jhansi
profiles.why: The fort of Rani Lakshmibai, and the railhead for Orchha.

gateways.name: Orchha
gateways.note: auto or bus from Jhansi, about half an hour

gateways.name: Datia Palace
gateways.note: on the Gwalior side; a stop on the way, not a day out

profiles.name: Orchha
profiles.why: A Bundela capital left almost to itself: cenotaphs on the river and painted palace rooms.

profiles.name: Gwalior
profiles.why: A hill fort above the city, and a palace whose Durbar Hall is a museum of its own.

profiles.name: Gorakhpur
profiles.why: The Gorakhnath temple city, and the railhead for Kushinagar.

gateways.name: Kushinagar
gateways.note: bus or taxi; where the Buddha attained mahaparinirvana

profiles.name: Haridwar
profiles.why: The Ganga leaves the hills here — the evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri is the whole point.

gateways.name: Rajaji National Park
gateways.note: shared jeep or taxi; mornings only in practice

profiles.name: Rishikesh
profiles.why: Yoga ashrams, rafting on the Ganga, and the road on towards the Garhwal hills.

profiles.name: Dehradun
profiles.why: A valley city between the Doon and the first ridge, with Mussoorie above it.

gateways.name: Mussoorie
gateways.note: shared taxi or bus up the ridge, about 1.5 h

profiles.name: Kathgodam (Nainital)
profiles.why: The railhead for the Kumaon lakes — Nainital is up the hill from here.

gateways.name: Nainital
gateways.note: taxi or bus up; about an hour from the station

gateways.name: Bhimtal and Sattal lakes
gateways.note: on the way up — worth breaking the journey

profiles.name: Ramnagar (Corbett)
profiles.why: The gate to Corbett National Park — tiger country in the Himalayan foothills.

gateways.name: Dhikala zone
gateways.note: permit and a forest vehicle; book well ahead

profiles.name: Shimla
profiles.why: The colonial summer capital on a ridge, reached by a mountain railway.

profiles.name: Kalka
profiles.why: Where the plains end and the Shimla toy train starts — a UNESCO mountain railway.

gateways.name: Shimla by toy train
gateways.note: the narrow-gauge service from this platform; book the window seats

profiles.name: Chandigarh
profiles.why: Le Corbusier’s planned city — the Capitol Complex is a World Heritage Site.

gateways.name: Pinjore Gardens
gateways.note: taxi towards Kalka; a Mughal garden on the way

profiles.name: Amritsar
profiles.why: The Golden Temple, open all night and free to every visitor, and a border ceremony nearby.

gateways.name: Wagah border ceremony
gateways.note: taxi or shared jeep; go early for the seating

profiles.name: Pathankot
profiles.why: The junction for the hills: Dharamshala, Dalhousie and the Kangra valley start here.

gateways.name: Dharamshala / McLeod Ganj
gateways.note: taxi or bus up; about 2.5 h

gateways.name: Dalhousie
gateways.note: taxi or bus; the road climbs from here

profiles.name: Jammu
profiles.why: The winter capital, and the railhead everyone uses before the climb to Vaishno Devi.

gateways.name: Katra / Vaishno Devi
gateways.note: taxi or bus to Katra, then the 12 km climb

profiles.name: Kurukshetra
profiles.why: The Mahabharata plain: Brahma Sarovar and the spot the Gita was spoken.

profiles.name: Alwar
profiles.why: A Rajput town under a hill fort, with Sariska’s tigers half an hour away.

gateways.name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
gateways.note: taxi or bus; safari vehicles from the gate

profiles.name: Moradabad
profiles.why: The brass city of the Ramganga — a working town, useful as a junction.

profiles.name: Saharanpur
profiles.why: Wood carving workshops and a Mughal-era garden, between Delhi and the hills.

profiles.name: Kolkata
profiles.why: The city that argues about everything, in a tram, over sweets — colonial monuments and a riverfront that still works.

gateways.name: Sundarbans
gateways.note: train to Canning or Sonarpur, then launch; an overnight, not a day trip

profiles.name: New Jalpaiguri (Siliguri)
profiles.why: The gateway to the eastern Himalaya: Darjeeling, Sikkim and the Dooars all start here.

gateways.name: Darjeeling
gateways.note: taxi or the toy train from NJP; about 3 h by road uphill

gateways.name: Gangtok
gateways.note: shared jeep or taxi; about 5 h, permits checked on the way

gateways.name: Kalimpong
gateways.note: shared jeep; quieter than Darjeeling and worth the drive

gateways.name: Dooars and Gorumara
gateways.note: taxi; forest lodges inside the reserve

profiles.name: Darjeeling
profiles.why: Tea gardens on a ridge with Kanchenjunga behind them, and a steam railway up the middle.

profiles.name: Patna
profiles.why: A river city older than most of Europe’s capitals, and the base for Bodh Gaya and Nalanda.

gateways.name: Bodh Gaya
gateways.note: better done from Gaya station, which is 13 km away

profiles.name: Gaya
profiles.why: The railhead for Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment.

gateways.name: Bodh Gaya
gateways.note: auto or bus; the temple complex is walkable once there

profiles.name: Rajgir
profiles.why: Hills, hot springs and the ruins of the first Buddhist monastery, in a valley that stayed quiet.

gateways.name: Nalanda ruins
gateways.note: auto or bus; the university ruins are the draw

profiles.name: Nalanda
profiles.why: The ruins of a monastic university that taught ten thousand students a thousand years ago.

profiles.name: Bhagalpur
profiles.why: A silk city on the Ganga, and the riverfront that goes with it.

profiles.name: Ranchi
profiles.why: Waterfalls and plateau forest at the edge of the Chota Nagpur — the base for Jharkhand’s falls.
profiles.best: Jul–Feb, best just after the monsoon

profiles.name: Jamshedpur
profiles.why: A company town built for a steel plant, with a hill of its own on the edge of it.

profiles.name: Deoghar
profiles.why: Baidyanath, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and one of India’s largest pilgrimage movements.

profiles.name: Dhanbad
profiles.why: Coal country — a working industrial landscape rather than a holiday one, but a major junction.

profiles.name: Bhubaneswar
profiles.why: The temple city of Kalinga architecture, with caves and a stupa on its edge.

gateways.name: Konark Sun Temple
gateways.note: taxi or bus; usually paired with Puri in one day

profiles.name: Puri
profiles.why: One of the four Char Dham towns, with a long beach and the Konark temple down the coast.

gateways.name: Konark Sun Temple
gateways.note: bus or taxi along the coast; a UNESCO site and a beach

gateways.name: Chilika Lake
gateways.note: train to Satapada side, then boat; dolphins in winter

profiles.name: Cuttack
profiles.why: An old river capital of Odisha, with a fort mound in the middle of it.

profiles.name: Bolpur (Shantiniketan)
profiles.why: Tagore’s university town, where classes are still held under trees.

profiles.name: Bishnupur
profiles.why: Terracotta temples: brickwork carved like ivory, in a town that was once a kingdom’s capital.

profiles.name: Murshidabad
profiles.why: The last independent Nawab’s capital: a palace, a thousand doors, and a river in front of it.

profiles.name: Malda
profiles.why: Mango country with two ruined capitals — Gaud and Pandua — in the fields around it.

profiles.name: Nabadwip Dham
profiles.why: The birthplace town of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, and a Krishna pilgrimage by the Ganga.

profiles.name: Digha
profiles.why: The closest sea beach to Kolkata — a broad, crowded, cheerful one.

profiles.name: Tarapith
profiles.why: A Shakti temple town on the Dwarka river, unusual even by Bengali pilgrimage standards.

profiles.name: Guwahati
profiles.why: The gateway to the North East, with a Shakti temple on a hill above the Brahmaputra.

gateways.name: Shillong
gateways.note: shared taxi or bus; about 3 h, and the road is the scenery

gateways.name: Kaziranga
gateways.note: better reached by train to Furkating or Jakhalabandha

profiles.name: Furkating (Kaziranga)
profiles.why: The railhead for Kaziranga: rhinos, elephants and grassland the size of a country.

gateways.name: Kaziranga ranges
gateways.note: taxi from the station; safaris are booked by range

profiles.name: Agartala
profiles.why: A palace, a lake and a border — Tripura’s capital, and now on the broad-gauge map.

profiles.name: Silchar
profiles.why: The Barak valley — tea, a river, and the long way round to the rest of the country.

profiles.name: Dimapur (Kohima)
profiles.why: The railhead for Nagaland — Kohima’s war cemetery and the Angami hills above it.

gateways.name: Kohima
gateways.note: shared taxi or bus; about 2.5 h up, permits for some areas

profiles.name: Jorhat
profiles.why: Tea research country, and the ferry point for Majuli — the largest river island anywhere.

gateways.name: Majuli island
gateways.note: taxi to Nimati ghat, then ferry; the ferry stops in low water

profiles.name: Dibrugarh
profiles.why: The end of the line in upper Assam: tea estates, the Brahmaputra, and rainforest beyond.

gateways.name: Namdapha and Arunachal
gateways.note: permits and a 4x4; plan it as its own trip

profiles.name: Mumbai
profiles.why: The sea on one side, Gothic and Art Deco on the other, and the best street food in the country.

gateways.name: Elephanta Caves
gateways.note: ferry from the Gateway of India, about an hour each way; boats stop in bad weather

gateways.name: Alibaug
gateways.note: ferry or road; a coastal weekend rather than a day trip

profiles.name: Pune
profiles.why: The Maratha capital: Peshwa palaces in the city and hill forts down every road out of it.

gateways.name: Lonavala and Karla Caves
gateways.note: train or road; the caves are a climb from the highway

profiles.name: Lonavala
profiles.why: A Sahyadri hill halt with the Karla and Bhaja cave complexes above it.
profiles.best: Jun–Sep for the monsoon, or Dec–Feb

profiles.name: Nashik
profiles.why: Temples on the Godavari, and the vineyards that made Indian wine a thing.

gateways.name: Trimbakeshwar
gateways.note: bus or taxi; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas

profiles.name: Shirdi
profiles.why: The Sai Baba temple — a pilgrimage town built entirely around one shrine.

profiles.name: Aurangabad
profiles.why: The base for both the Ajanta and Ellora cave complexes, which deserve separate days.

gateways.name: Ellora Caves
gateways.note: taxi or bus; half a day of walking

gateways.name: Ajanta Caves
gateways.note: taxi or the morning bus; a full day out, and closed on Mondays

profiles.name: Nagpur
profiles.why: The orange city at the centre of the country, with tigers and hill stations around it.

gateways.name: Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve
gateways.note: a separate trip; stay near Chandrapur, not Nagpur

profiles.name: Kolhapur
profiles.why: The Mahalaxmi temple, its own fierce chilli-and-jaggery food, and Panhala fort above.

gateways.name: Panhala Fort
gateways.note: bus or taxi up the ghat; half a day

profiles.name: Mahabaleshwar (via Wathar)
profiles.why: Strawberry country on the crest of the Sahyadris, with valley views on both sides.

gateways.name: Mahabaleshwar from Wathar
gateways.note: bus or taxi; the climb takes about 2 h

gateways.name: Satara town
gateways.note: from Satara station it is the same road, slightly shorter

profiles.name: Ratnagiri
profiles.why: The Konkan coast at its calmest, with Alphonso mangoes and a cliff-top fort.

gateways.name: Ganpatipule
gateways.note: auto or bus along the coast

profiles.name: Goa
profiles.why: Beaches within a short ride of every station, plus Portuguese churches and a spice hinterland.

sights.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus, Old Goa

gateways.name: Dudhsagar Falls
gateways.note: jeep from Kulem, which is itself a station; closed in peak monsoon

gateways.name: Spice plantations, Ponda
gateways.note: taxi; usually combined with Old Goa

profiles.name: Ahmedabad
profiles.why: Indo-Saracenic city of stepwells, the Sabarmati Ashram, and a night market worth planning around.

gateways.name: Modhera Sun Temple and Rani ki Vav
gateways.note: a full-day drive; both are World Heritage Sites

profiles.name: Vadodara
profiles.why: A palace that still has its own railway station, and a World Heritage city half an hour away.

gateways.name: Statue of Unity, Kevadiya
gateways.note: a long day out by road; better as an overnight

profiles.name: Surat
profiles.why: Diamond and textile money, a Dutch and English trading past, and beaches out along the coast.

profiles.name: Dwarka
profiles.why: Krishna’s city at the western edge of the country — a temple town by the sea.

profiles.name: Somnath
profiles.why: The first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, rebuilt six times, with the sea behind it.

gateways.name: Veraval harbour
gateways.note: auto; the fishing port next door

profiles.name: Junagadh and Gir
profiles.why: An old princely city under Girnar hill, with the last Asiatic lions an hour away.

gateways.name: Sasan Gir
gateways.note: there is a small station at Sasan Gir itself; safaris need booking

profiles.name: Bhuj
profiles.why: Kutch: white desert at full moon, mirrorwork craft villages, and a palace full of it.

gateways.name: Great Rann of Kutch
gateways.note: taxi; the salt desert is the reason to come

profiles.name: Palitana
profiles.why: A hill covered in Jain temples, reached by six hundred steps.

profiles.name: Rajkot
profiles.why: A Kathiawar trading city, and a convenient base between Gir and the Kutch.

profiles.name: Jaipur
profiles.why: The pink city: a hill fort above, and a palace, an observatory and a bazaar in a walkable line.

gateways.name: Nahargarh and Jaigarh
gateways.note: taxi up the ridge; sunset from above Amber

profiles.name: Jodhpur
profiles.why: The blue city under Mehrangarh, with the desert at its back.

sights.name: Sardar Market and the clock tower

gateways.name: Osian temples
gateways.note: taxi; a desert-outpost detour in the afternoon

profiles.name: Jaisalmer
profiles.why: A living fort of yellow stone in the middle of the Thar, with dunes an hour out.

gateways.name: Sam Sand Dunes
gateways.note: taxi or jeep; camel rides and sunset, or a desert camp night

profiles.name: Bikaner
profiles.why: A walled desert city with a fort that was never taken, and the rats of Karni Mata nearby.

gateways.name: Karni Mata, Deshnoke
gateways.note: bus or taxi; the temple of the rats, an hour out

profiles.name: Ajmer
profiles.why: The Sufi dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, with Pushkar’s lake just over the hill.

gateways.name: Pushkar
gateways.note: auto or bus; the Brahma temple and the lake ghats

profiles.name: Abu Road (Mount Abu)
profiles.why: The only hill station in Rajasthan, with Jain temples in marble at Dilwara.

gateways.name: Mount Abu from Abu Road
gateways.note: taxi or bus up the ghat road, about an hour

profiles.name: Chittaurgarh
profiles.why: The fort every Rajput story measures itself against, spread over a whole hill.

profiles.name: Kota
profiles.why: A river city with a palace on the Chambal, halfway between Delhi and Mumbai.

gateways.name: Bundi
gateways.note: short train or taxi; the stepwells and the palace are better than Kota’s

profiles.name: Sawai Madhopur (Ranthambore)
profiles.why: The tiger reserve with a fort inside it, and a tenth-century town beside the gate.

gateways.name: Park zones
gateways.note: safaris are booked per zone and sell out; the station is the base

profiles.name: Bharatpur
profiles.why: A bird sanctuary that is a World Heritage Site, on the road to Fatehpur Sikri.

profiles.name: Bhopal
profiles.why: Two lakes, a Begum’s city, and the Buddhist stupas of Sanchi down the road.

gateways.name: Sanchi Stupa
gateways.note: train or taxi; the stop for it is Sanchi, one stop before Bhopal

profiles.name: Sanchi
profiles.why: The Great Stupa, the oldest stone structure in the country, in a quiet hillside complex.

profiles.name: Indore
profiles.why: The cleanest city in the country, and the best reason to stop eating elsewhere in Madhya Pradesh.

gateways.name: Mandu
gateways.note: a full day by road, or a night there; the monsoon is its season

gateways.name: Omkareshwar
gateways.note: train to Omkareshwar Road, 10 km short, then auto

profiles.name: Omkareshwar
profiles.why: A Jyotirlinga on an island in the Narmada, shaped like the symbol it is named for.

profiles.name: Ujjain
profiles.why: Mahakaleshwar and the Shipra ghats — one of the four Kumbh cities.

profiles.name: Jabalpur
profiles.why: Marble cliffs over the Narmada, with the Dhuandhar falls in the same afternoon.

gateways.name: Bhedaghat
gateways.note: auto or bus; boat rides on the Narmada run in season

profiles.name: Khajuraho
profiles.why: Chandela temples covered in sculpture, on the World Heritage list for it.

gateways.name: Raneh Falls
gateways.note: taxi; a canyon of pink granite in season

gateways.name: Panna National Park
gateways.note: taxi; tigers and the Ken river

profiles.name: Pipariya (Pachmarhi)
profiles.why: The railhead for Pachmarhi, the hill station in the Satpura range.

gateways.name: Pachmarhi
gateways.note: bus or taxi up the ghats, about 1.5 h

profiles.name: Raipur
profiles.why: The capital of Chhattisgarh, and the junction towards the waterfalls of Bastar.

profiles.name: Jagdalpur
profiles.why: Bastar — tribal country with waterfalls, caves and a very different India.

gateways.name: Chitrakote and Tirathgarh falls
gateways.note: taxi or bus; the river is at its widest just after the monsoon

profiles.name: Chennai
profiles.why: A long city beach, Dravidian temples, and the best filter coffee in the country.

gateways.name: Mahabalipuram
gateways.note: bus or taxi down the coast road; the shore temples are a UNESCO site

gateways.name: Pulicat Lake
gateways.note: taxi; flamingos in winter

profiles.name: Chengalpattu (Mahabalipuram)
profiles.why: The railhead for the Pallava shore temples at Mahabalipuram.

gateways.name: Mahabalipuram
gateways.note: bus or auto from the station; half an hour

profiles.name: Kanchipuram
profiles.why: One of the seven sacred cities, with silk saris woven in the same streets as the temples.

profiles.name: Puducherry
profiles.why: French-grid streets with mustard-yellow walls, behind a promenade on the Bay of Bengal.

gateways.name: Auroville
gateways.note: auto or bus; the Matrimandir needs a booking to go inside

gateways.name: Paradise Beach
gateways.note: ferry from the Chunnambar backwater

profiles.name: Thanjavur
profiles.why: The Chola capital: the Big Temple is a thousand years old and still the tallest of its kind.

gateways.name: Darasuram Airavatesvara Temple
gateways.note: bus or taxi; the third of the Great Living Chola Temples

gateways.name: Kumbakonam
gateways.note: a short train ride; better as its own stop

profiles.name: Kumbakonam
profiles.why: A Mahamaham tank ringed by temples, with two Chola masterpieces within half an hour.

gateways.name: Darasuram
gateways.note: auto; the Airavatesvara temple is a UNESCO site

gateways.name: Swamimalai and Patteeswaram
gateways.note: auto; bronze casting workshops beside the temples

profiles.name: Chidambaram
profiles.why: The Nataraja temple, where Shiva is worshipped as the dancer.

gateways.name: Pichavaram
gateways.note: bus or auto; boat through the mangrove channels

profiles.name: Tiruchirappalli
profiles.why: A rock fort you climb by steps cut in the rock, and the great Srirangam temple island.

profiles.name: Madurai
profiles.why: The Meenakshi temple, and a city that has organised its life around it for two thousand years.

gateways.name: Thiruparankundram and Alagar Kovil
gateways.note: bus or auto; rock-cut temples on the edge of the city

profiles.name: Rameswaram
profiles.why: A temple town on an island, reached by a bridge over the sea, with a beach on both sides.

gateways.name: Dhanushkodi
gateways.note: taxi; the road ends at the water, ruins on the way

profiles.name: Kanyakumari
profiles.why: The southern tip: sunrise and sunset over three seas, with a temple on the shore.

profiles.name: Tirunelveli
profiles.why: A temple city on the Thamirabarani, with the Western Ghats and the coast both close.

gateways.name: Manimuthar Falls and Kalakkad
gateways.note: taxi; hill forest on the Ghats edge

profiles.name: Mettupalayam and Coonoor
profiles.why: The Nilgiri mountain railway: a rack line that climbs from the plains into the tea hills.

gateways.name: Ooty (Udhagamandalam)
gateways.note: the same toy train continues up, or bus over the ghat road

profiles.name: Coimbatore
profiles.why: A textile city under the Ghats gap, with the Adiyogi statue on its edge.

gateways.name: Isha Yoga Center
gateways.note: taxi; the statue is lit at night

profiles.name: Kodaikanal Road
profiles.why: The railhead for Kodaikanal, up on the Palani hills.

gateways.name: Kodaikanal
gateways.note: bus or taxi up the ghats; about 2.5 h from the station

profiles.name: Tirupati
profiles.why: The Venkateswara temple at Tirumala, the busiest pilgrimage in the world by footfall.

gateways.name: Tirumala
gateways.note: bus or the walking path; darshan tokens are the thing to arrange

profiles.name: Vijayawada
profiles.why: A Krishna river city with a temple on a hill and caves across the water.

profiles.name: Visakhapatnam
profiles.why: Beaches and a harbour with the Eastern Ghats falling into the sea behind them.

gateways.name: Araku Valley
gateways.note: the train through the ghats to Araku is the excursion; go and come back the same day

gateways.name: Borra Caves
gateways.note: usually combined with the Araku train or a taxi

profiles.name: Warangal
profiles.why: A Kakatiya capital with a fort, a lake and a temple whose pillars are carved through.

gateways.name: Ramappa Temple
gateways.note: taxi; the Kakatiya temple that joined the World Heritage list

gateways.name: Pakhal Lake
gateways.note: taxi; a Kakatiya reservoir in the forest

profiles.name: Hyderabad
profiles.why: Biryani, pearls, and four hundred years of Deccan architecture in one old city.

gateways.name: Ramoji Film City
gateways.note: taxi; a full day, and it is not really the city

profiles.name: Bengaluru
profiles.why: A garden city that turned into a tech city and kept the weather, the dosas and the parks.

gateways.name: Nandi Hills
gateways.note: taxi, ideally before dawn for the sunrise

gateways.name: Mysuru
gateways.note: a fast train from the city; a day trip that deserves two

profiles.name: Mysuru
profiles.why: The palace, and a city that kept its own calendar of festivals and its own food.

gateways.name: Srirangapatna
gateways.note: bus or auto; Tipu Sultan’s island capital

gateways.name: Coorg (Madikeri)
gateways.note: road only, and worth two nights rather than a day trip

profiles.name: Hospet (Hampi)
profiles.why: The railhead for Hampi, a boulder landscape full of a ruined empire.

gateways.name: Hampi
gateways.note: auto or bus from Hospet; bicycles are the usual way around the ruins

profiles.name: Badami
profiles.why: Cave temples cut into red sandstone cliffs above a lake, with two more capitals nearby.

gateways.name: Pattadakal
gateways.note: bus or auto; a UNESCO site of Chalukyan temples

gateways.name: Aihole
gateways.note: usually paired with Pattadakal in one taxi

profiles.name: Hassan (Belur and Halebidu)
profiles.why: Hoysala temples where the stone is carved so finely it looks turned on a lathe.

gateways.name: Belur and Halebidu
gateways.note: bus or taxi; the two are usually done in one day

gateways.name: Shravanabelagola
gateways.note: on the Bengaluru side, so stop on the way in

profiles.name: Udupi
profiles.why: A temple town that gave the world its own cuisine, with a beach a bus ride away.

gateways.name: St Mary’s Island
gateways.note: boat from Malpe; the basalt columns are the sight

profiles.name: Mangaluru
profiles.why: A port city of red-tiled roofs, beaches north and south, and its own very good food.

profiles.name: Murdeshwar and Gokarna
profiles.why: The Karnataka coast: a giant Shiva statue by the sea, then a temple town with empty beaches.

profiles.name: Karwar
profiles.why: A quiet harbour town between the Kali river and the sea, where Tagore once stayed.

profiles.name: Kadur (Chikmagalur)
profiles.why: The railhead for coffee country in the Baba Budangiri hills.

gateways.name: Chikmagalur
gateways.note: bus or taxi; the ghat road starts climbing here

profiles.name: Hubballi
profiles.why: A junction city in the northern plateau, useful as a base for Badami and Hampi.

profiles.name: Bijapur
profiles.why: The Gol Gumbaz, whose whispering gallery is worth the trip on its own.

profiles.name: Kalaburagi (Gulbarga)
profiles.why: A Bahmani capital with a great mosque and a fort, off most itineraries.

profiles.name: Kochi
profiles.why: Chinese fishing nets, a Portuguese church and a Jewish quarter, all in one small peninsula.

sights.name: Fort Kochi and the Chinese fishing nets

gateways.name: Alappuzha backwaters
gateways.note: train or road; houseboats start from Alappuzha, not Kochi

gateways.name: Munnar
gateways.note: road only; better done from Aluva, which is on the rail line

profiles.name: Aluva (Munnar)
profiles.why: The railhead people use for Munnar, up in the tea hills of the Western Ghats.

gateways.name: Munnar
gateways.note: bus or taxi up; about 4 h on a winding road

profiles.name: Alappuzha
profiles.why: Backwater country: houseboats, canals, and a beach along the sandbar behind them.

profiles.name: Kollam and Varkala
profiles.why: The start of the backwater route south, and a cliff beach at Varkala below it.

gateways.name: Varkala
gateways.note: it has its own station, four stops south of Kollam

profiles.name: Thiruvananthapuram
profiles.why: The Padmanabhaswamy temple, colonial museums, and beaches on both sides of the city.

gateways.name: Kovalam
gateways.note: bus or auto; the lighthouse beach is the quiet end

profiles.name: Kozhikode
profiles.why: Where Vasco da Gama landed, and where the Malabar coast eats best.

gateways.name: Wayanad
gateways.note: taxi or bus up the ghats; a hill district rather than a town

profiles.name: Kannur
profiles.why: Theyyam country: ritual dance, cliff beaches and a fort on the Malabar coast.

profiles.name: Thrissur
profiles.why: The cultural capital of Kerala, and the home of the Pooram festival.

gateways.name: Athirappilly
gateways.note: taxi; the falls are at their best right after the monsoon

profiles.name: Guruvayur
profiles.why: One of the most visited Krishna temples in the south, in a town built around it.

profiles.name: Palakkad
profiles.why: The gap in the Western Ghats — the road and rail pass through it, and the hills are on both sides.

gateways.name: Silent Valley
gateways.note: permit and a forest vehicle; the station is the nearest rail point
